question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The situation was out of hand. So, the manager called the police station for help.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To be uncontrollable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "out of hand" means out of control; no longer manageable. This is why the manager had to call the police. (नियंत्रण से बाहर / बेकाबू)

◦ Example: The protest turned violent and got completely out of hand.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "serious", Option 2 "in an undecided state" and Option 4 "abrupt" do not capture the sense of being uncontrollable.

NOTE

• "Out of hand" also means "immediately/without thought" (he rejected the idea out of hand). Similar idioms of losing control: "get out of control", "go haywire", "spiral out of control".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Foremost
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Unimportant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Foremost" means most important, leading or ranking first. Its antonym is "unimportant", meaning of little significance. (सर्वप्रमुख का विलोम — महत्वहीन)

◦ Example: He is the foremost expert in his field, whereas the trainee's opinion was seen as unimportant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Disposed" (inclined / got rid of), Option 2 "Forecast" (prediction) and Option 4 "Premature" (too early) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of foremost: leading, chief, principal, primary, prime.

• Antonyms: unimportant, insignificant, minor, secondary.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

This is going to be overwhelming for you as you have taken on work beyond your capabilities.
option_3: bitten off more than you can chew
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. bitten off more than you can chew.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to bite off more than one can chew" means to take on more work or responsibility than one can handle. It exactly replaces "taken on work beyond your capabilities". (क्षमता से अधिक काम लेना)

◦ Example: By agreeing to three projects at once, he has bitten off more than he can chew.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "at the eleventh hour" — at the last moment.

• Option 2 "called it a day" — to stop working for the day.

• Option 4 "put something on ice" — to postpone / put on hold.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of overburdening: "to spread oneself too thin", "to have too much on one's plate", "to be in over one's head".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

My mother asked me who did accompany me to the airport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. who accompanied me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is an indirect (reported) question, so it should follow the statement word order (subject + verb) without the auxiliary "did". The correct past-tense form is "who accompanied me".

◦ Correct: My mother asked me who accompanied me to the airport.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "who must accompanied me" wrongly uses "must + past".

• Option 3 "who accompany me" is present tense (wrong tense).

• Option 4 "whom I was accompanied" changes the meaning and is grammatically wrong.

NOTE

• In reported/indirect questions, do not use "do/does/did" and do not invert: "She asked where I lived" (not "where did I live"). The question mark is also dropped.

question:
The given sentence is divided into four parts. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

He was acquitted to / a cyber crime / on the basis of evidence / given to the court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He was acquitted to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "acquit" takes the preposition "of", not "to". "To acquit someone of a charge/crime" means to declare them not guilty.

◦ Correct: He was acquitted of a cyber crime on the basis of evidence given to the court.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "a cyber crime", "on the basis of evidence" and "given to the court" are all correct.

NOTE

• Verb + preposition collocations for SSC: acquitted of, accused of, charged with, convicted of, guilty of, innocent of.

question: Select the option that has an error in the use of phrasal verb.
option_1: Back up your essential files. Technology is only sometimes reliable.
option_2: Pushpa came across an old photo in the album and asked me to recognise the face in it.
option_3: Please turn up the heater. The weather is too cold today.
option_4: Please suggest me some tips to get out nervousness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Please suggest me some tips to get out nervousness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb to mean "overcome/recover from" a feeling is "get over", not "get out". Also, it needs the preposition — "get over nervousness".

◦ Correct: Please suggest some tips to get over nervousness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "back up" (make a copy), Option 2 "came across" (found by chance) and Option 3 "turn up" (increase) are all used correctly.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "get": get over (recover from), get out (leave/escape), get on (progress/board), get through (finish/pass), get by (manage).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Leif Erikson is a Viking _______ believed to have sailed from the Green Lands to Vinland. Vinland is now thought to be the northern tip of Canada's Newfoundland island where _______ found evidence of Erikson's _______ in 1960s.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. explorer; archaeologists; settlement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is about a Viking who sailed and discovered new land, so he was an "explorer". Those who dig up and study ancient remains are "archaeologists", and the evidence they found was of Erikson's "settlement" (a place where people settled).

◦ Correct: ... a Viking explorer ... where archaeologists found evidence of Erikson's settlement in the 1960s.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 mismatch at least one blank (e.g., "sailor + excavators + packed", "astronomer", "calligrapher" do not fit the exploration-and-archaeology context).

NOTE

• In fill-in-the-blank passages, use the overall theme (here, Viking exploration and archaeological discovery) to choose the set of words that fits all blanks logically.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

The new syllabus of Final Semester of MBA is very difficult.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. easy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Difficult" means hard to do or understand. Its antonym is "easy", meaning simple and not hard. (कठिन का विलोम — आसान)

◦ Example: The first question was difficult, but the last one was quite easy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "perplexing" (confusing) and Option 4 "problematical" (full of problems) are synonyms of difficult.

• Option 2 "rigid" (stiff/inflexible) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of difficult: hard, tough, arduous, complicated, challenging.

• Antonyms: easy, simple, effortless, straightforward.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Defecteev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Defecteev" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Defective", meaning having a fault or flaw; imperfect. (दोषपूर्ण / खराब)

◦ Example: The shop replaced the defective phone free of charge.

• Spelling key: DE + FEC + TIVE — ends in "-tive" (like active, effective, creative).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Crowded", "Elegant" and "Efficient" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: defect (noun), defective (adjective), defection (noun). Adjectives ending in "-tive": defective, effective, attractive, sensitive.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

This sentence can have multiple meanings. Could you please specify what it means?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ambiguous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A phrase or sentence that "can have multiple meanings" is said to be "ambiguous" — open to more than one interpretation. (अस्पष्ट / द्विअर्थी)

◦ Example: The ambiguous instructions confused everyone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Homogeneous" (uniform / of the same kind) and Option 4 "Heterogeneous" (of different kinds) refer to composition, not meaning.

• Option 2 "Amorphous" (shapeless) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ambiguous: vague, unclear, equivocal, obscure. Antonyms: clear, explicit, unambiguous, definite.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

One of the most horrified serials of the Indian television industry was broadcast twenty years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. most horrifying serials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Horrifying" (present participle) is an active adjective meaning "causing horror", which correctly describes the serials. "Horrified" (past participle) describes a person who feels horror, so it is wrong for the serials.

◦ Correct: One of the most horrifying serials ... was broadcast twenty years ago.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "most horror serials" is awkward; Option 3 keeps the wrong "horrified"; Option 4 "more horrify serials" is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• "-ing" adjectives describe the thing causing the feeling (a boring film, an exciting match, a horrifying scene); "-ed" adjectives describe the person feeling it (a bored student, an excited fan, a horrified viewer).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She is studying / the medicine / at university / to become a doctor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the medicine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When "medicine" refers to the subject/field of study in general, it is used without the article "the". Hence it should be "studying medicine", not "the medicine".

◦ Correct: She is studying medicine at university to become a doctor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "She is studying", "at university" and "to become a doctor" are all correct.

NOTE

• Names of subjects, meals, languages and general activities take no article: study medicine/history/English, have breakfast, play football. Use "the" only when referring to a specific medicine (the medicine the doctor prescribed).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The gold watch / look really expensive / and is not affordable / for common people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. look really expensive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "The gold watch" is singular, so the verb must be singular — "looks", not "look".

◦ Correct: The gold watch looks really expensive and is not affordable for common people.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "The gold watch", "and is not affordable" and "for common people" are all correct (note "is not affordable" already correctly uses the singular "is").

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: a singular subject takes a singular verb (watch looks, he runs). The later clause "is not affordable" confirms the subject is singular.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the given word.

Fusion
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Blend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fusion" means the process of joining or merging two or more things into one. Its closest synonym is "blend" (a mixture formed by combining things). (संलयन / मिश्रण)

◦ Example: This music is a fusion/blend of jazz and Indian classical styles.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Grind" (to crush), Option 2 "Glide" (to move smoothly) and Option 3 "Ingredient" (a component) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fusion: blend, merger, union, amalgamation, combination.

• In science, "nuclear fusion" is the joining of atomic nuclei (the process that powers the Sun).

question:
Rectify the following sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the underlined word from the options.

Life is a collection of ephmeral moments.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ephemeral.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Ephemeral", meaning lasting for a very short time; short-lived. (क्षणभंगुर / अल्पकालिक)

◦ Example: The beauty of a rainbow is ephemeral.

• Spelling key: E + PHE + ME + RAL — note the "ph" (which sounds like "f").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 ("Epmeral", "Ephameral", "Ephemerl") are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ephemeral: transient, fleeting, momentary, short-lived, transitory.

• Antonyms: permanent, everlasting, enduring, perpetual.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

His decision to quit his stable job and travel the world was driven by a sudden caprice.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Impulse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Caprice" means a sudden and unaccountable change of mood or behaviour; a whim. Its closest synonym is "impulse" (a sudden urge to act). (सनक / तरंग)

◦ Example: On a caprice/impulse, she bought a ticket and flew to Goa.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Sorrow" (sadness), Option 3 "Delight" (great pleasure) and Option 4 "Determination" (firm resolve) do not mean a sudden whim.

NOTE

• Synonyms of caprice: whim, impulse, fancy, notion, quirk. The adjective is "capricious" (given to sudden changes of mood).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Restraint
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Self-control.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Restraint" means self-control; the act of holding back or keeping one's feelings/actions under control. Its closest synonym is "self-control". (संयम / आत्म-नियंत्रण)

◦ Example: He showed great restraint/self-control by not reacting to the insult.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Self-esteem" (self-respect), Option 2 "Self-acceptance" and Option 3 "Self-appraisal" (self-evaluation) are different concepts.

NOTE

• Synonyms of restraint: self-control, self-discipline, moderation, restriction, control.

• Antonyms: indulgence, excess, abandon.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Explaination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Explaination" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Explanation", meaning a statement that makes something clear. (व्याख्या / स्पष्टीकरण)

◦ Example: The teacher gave a clear explanation of the theorem.

• Spelling key: EX + PLA + NA + TION — there is no "i" after "expla" (it is "explanation", though the verb is "explain").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Proposal", "Myriad" (a countless number) and "Accolades" (awards/praise) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Note the change: the verb "explain" has an "i", but the noun "explanation" drops it. Similarly: pronounce → pronunciation.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

It has been / noticed that / across all his faults, / he is admired.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. across all his faults.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To express a contrast ("even though he has faults, he is admired"), the correct preposition is "despite / in spite of", not "across". "Across" means "on the other side / from one side to another" and does not fit.

◦ Correct: It has been noticed that despite all his faults, he is admired.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "It has been", "noticed that" and "he is admired" are all correct.

NOTE

• Contrast prepositions: despite / in spite of + noun (despite his faults). For a clause, use although / though / even though (although he has faults).

question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Bilingual children are so intelligent than those who speak just one language.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. more intelligent than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. As "intelligent" is a long (multi-syllable) adjective, its comparative is formed with "more" — "more intelligent than".

◦ Correct: Bilingual children are more intelligent than those who speak just one language.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "better intelligent than" wrongly combines "better" with "intelligent".

• Option 2 "the most intelligent to" is superlative with a wrong preposition.

• Option 4 "so intelligent to" keeps the wrong "so" and uses the wrong preposition.

NOTE

• Long adjectives (2+ syllables) form the comparative with "more ... than" (more intelligent than, more beautiful than) and the superlative with "the most" (the most intelligent).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1)_______ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2)_______ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3)_______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4)_______ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. modern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The newspaper is a feature of the present-day world, so it is a sign of "modern" civilisation (present-day, up-to-date). (आधुनिक)

◦ Correct: The newspaper is one of the significant signs of modern civilisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "prehistoric" (before written records) and Option 4 "ancient" (very old) contradict the modern nature of newspapers.

• Option 3 "monolithic" (large, uniform and rigid) does not fit "civilisation" here.

NOTE

• "Modern" = of the present or recent times. Synonyms: contemporary, current, present-day. Antonyms: ancient, old, prehistoric.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1)_______ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2)_______ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3)_______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4)_______ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. present.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The newspaper is the most popular form of reading now, so "present times" is correct — it refers to the current era. (वर्तमान समय)

◦ Correct: It is the most popular form of reading in the present times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "future" and Option 4 "past" contradict the current relevance.

• Option 2 "dark" ("dark times") changes the meaning to a period of trouble, which does not fit.

NOTE

• "Present times / present day" = the current period. This links with blank 1 ("modern"), keeping the passage in the here-and-now.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1)_______ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2)_______ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3)_______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4)_______ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. both.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correlative conjunction "both ... and" is used to join two positive items. Here a newspaper keeps us "both entertained and informed". (दोनों ... और)

◦ Correct: A newspaper keeps us both entertained and informed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "either" pairs with "or" (either ... or), Option 4 "nor" pairs with "neither" — neither fits "___ entertained and informed".

• Option 3 "or" alone does not fit the "___ ... and" structure.

NOTE

• Correlative conjunctions (come in pairs): both ... and, either ... or, neither ... nor, not only ... but also, whether ... or.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1)_______ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2)_______ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3)_______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4)_______ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence stresses the power of public opinion — that not even one government can resist strong public opinion for long. So "No government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion." (कोई भी नहीं)

◦ Correct: No government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "All", 3 "Both" and 4 "Some" would reverse or weaken the intended meaning (that governments cannot withstand public opinion).

NOTE

• "No + singular noun + can ..." is a strong negative generalisation (No man is an island). The context (press/public opinion controlling the government) requires this emphatic "No".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1)_______ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2)_______ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3)_______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4)_______ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. together.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The press acts as an interpreter between the rulers and the ruled and brings them closer / unites them — hence "brings the rulers and the ruled together". (एक साथ लाना)

◦ Correct: ... brings the rulers and the ruled together.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "apart" (separated) is the opposite of the intended sense.

• Option 2 "overall" (in general) and Option 4 "jointed" (connected by joints) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Bring together" is a phrasal verb meaning to unite people or make them cooperate. Opposite: "drive apart / set apart".

question: Which event brought about a profound change in Ashoka's administrative policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Kalinga War.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) brought about a profound change in Emperor Ashoka's policy. Shocked by the immense bloodshed and suffering, Ashoka gave up further wars of conquest (Bherighosha) and adopted a policy of peace, welfare and moral conquest (Dhammaghosha). (कलिंग युद्ध — अशोक की नीति में परिवर्तन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Kalinga War is described in Rock Edict XIII. After it, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and worked for the welfare of his subjects, appointing Dhamma Mahamatras to spread moral values.

• He sent missionaries, including his children Mahinda and Sanghamitta, to Sri Lanka (Ceylon).

NOTE

• Ashoka is called "Devanampiya Piyadasi" in his inscriptions. His edicts were deciphered by James Prinsep (1837).

question: Under which of the following Acts, was Warren Hastings appointed as the Governor-General of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Regulating Act, 1773.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the "Governor-General of Bengal", and Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट 1773 — वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Regulating Act was the first step by the British Parliament to control the affairs of the East India Company; it also established a Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

• The Charter Act of 1833 later made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck being the first).

NOTE

• Sequence of key Acts: Regulating Act (1773) → Pitt's India Act (1784) → Charter Acts (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853) → Government of India Act (1858, 1919, 1935).

question:
While estimating Gross Domestic Product, the monetary value of only final goods are considered because __________.

a. its immobility, the active economic flow is ended.  b. of the issues of double counting  c. the value added at each stage of the production process is included
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• While estimating GDP, only the value of final goods and services is counted (not intermediate goods) to avoid the problem of "double counting" — statement b is correct. (दोहरी गणना से बचने हेतु — केवल अंतिम वस्तुएँ)

◦ If we counted both intermediate and final goods, the same value would be added more than once.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• An alternative method that gives the same result is the value-added method, which sums the value added at each stage (this avoids double counting differently), but the question's stated reason for counting only final goods is to prevent double counting.

• GDP = the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period.

NOTE

• Methods of measuring national income: Product/Value-added method, Income method, Expenditure method. Intermediate goods are excluded to prevent double counting.

question: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built during the reign of the __________ king Narasimhavarman II.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Tamil Nadu, was built during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) in the early 8th century. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. (शोर मंदिर — पल्लव राजवंश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mahabalipuram was a major port city of the Pallavas and is famous for its rathas (monolithic temples), cave temples and rock-cut sculptures (e.g., "Descent of the Ganga / Arjuna's Penance").

• The Pallava capital was Kanchipuram.

NOTE

• The Pallavas were pioneers of Dravidian temple architecture. The Kailasanatha Temple (Kanchipuram) was also built by Narasimhavarman II.

question: As on February 2024, Yanthungo Patton is the Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As on February 2024, Yanthungo Patton (Y. Patton) was the Deputy Chief Minister of Nagaland. (नागालैंड के उप-मुख्यमंत्री — वाई. पैटन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nagaland became a state on 1 December 1963; its capital is Kohima.

• Nagaland is famous for the Hornbill Festival (the "Festival of Festivals"), celebrated in December.

NOTE

• Nagaland is one of the "Seven Sisters" states of North-East India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya).

question: Which of the following is a mineral deficiency disease?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goitre.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Goitre" is a mineral deficiency disease caused by the deficiency of iodine, leading to the swelling of the thyroid gland in the neck. (घेंघा रोग — आयोडीन की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rickets — caused by deficiency of Vitamin D (softening/weakening of bones).

• Scurvy — caused by deficiency of Vitamin C (bleeding gums).

• Marasmus — a form of protein-energy malnutrition in children.

NOTE

• Iodine is added to common salt (iodised salt) to prevent goitre. Other mineral-deficiency issues: anaemia (iron) and weak bones/teeth (calcium).

question: Sekrenyi festival of Nagaland is celebrated annually in the month of _______ as part of the Mini Hornbill Tribal Festival which is a celebration of purification accompanied with feasting and singing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is February.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Sekrenyi (Sekrenye) festival" of the Angami Naga tribe of Nagaland is celebrated annually in February. It is a festival of purification and sanctification, marked by feasting, singing and rituals. (सेक्रेनी महोत्सव — फरवरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Sekrenyi" means "sanctification festival"; it is also called Phousanyi.

• Nagaland's biggest festival is the Hornbill Festival, held in December at Kisama.

NOTE

• Festivals of Nagaland: Sekrenyi (Angami), Moatsu (Ao), Tuluni (Sumi), Aoleang (Konyak) and the state-wide Hornbill Festival.

question: Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer who had been honoured with Padma Shri award for 2020, is associated with which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer and guru honoured with the Padma Shri (2020), is associated with Madhya Pradesh (he is a leading exponent of the Kathak tradition and has trained many dancers). (पुरुषोत्तम दाधीच — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He is credited with popularising Kathak and blending it with other styles; he is associated with the Raigarh gharana tradition of Kathak.

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms, mainly of North and Central India.

NOTE

• Major Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh. Famous Kathak dancers: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Kumudini Lakhia.

question: What does WFI stand for in the context of sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wrestling Federation of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the context of sports, "WFI" stands for the "Wrestling Federation of India", the national governing body for the sport of wrestling in India. (भारतीय कुश्ती महासंघ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The WFI is affiliated to the international wrestling body United World Wrestling (UWW).

• India has produced Olympic wrestling medallists such as Sushil Kumar, Yogeshwar Dutt, Sakshi Malik, Bajrang Punia and Ravi Kumar Dahiya.

NOTE

• Some sports federations for SSC: BCCI (cricket), AIFF (football), AITA (tennis), BAI (badminton), HI (hockey).

question: The architectural marvels, temples of Gangaikonda-Cholapuram, were built by which of the following king?
solution_text:
The correct answer is King Rajendra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The temples of Gangaikonda Cholapuram were built by the Chola king Rajendra I (Rajendra Chola I) to commemorate his victorious military campaign up to the Ganga river in the north. (गंगईकोंड चोलपुरम — राजेंद्र चोल प्रथम)

• The Brihadeeswarar (Gangaikonda Cholapuram) Temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (part of the "Great Living Chola Temples").

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rajendra Chola I made Gangaikonda Cholapuram his new capital and took the title "Gangaikonda Chola" (the Chola who conquered the Ganga).

• The Cholas had a powerful navy and expanded their influence to Southeast Asia (Srivijaya).

NOTE

• Vijayalaya founded the Chola dynasty; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur. Mahendravarman was a Pallava king.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a 'Lagoon'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nainital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nainital" is a freshwater lake in the Kumaon Himalayas of Uttarakhand — it is NOT a lagoon. A lagoon is a shallow body of water separated from the sea by a sandbar or coral reef. (नैनीताल — झील, लैगून नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chilika (Odisha) — the largest coastal lagoon in India (a brackish-water lagoon).

• Pulicat (Andhra Pradesh/Tamil Nadu) — the second-largest lagoon in India.

• Kolleru (Andhra Pradesh) — a large freshwater lake, often grouped with lagoons.

NOTE

• Lagoons are usually brackish (a mix of fresh and salt water) and are important habitats for birds and fish. Chilika is famous for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins.

question: Dappu dance is a famous dance form of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dappu" is a vigorous folk dance of Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), performed to the beat of a percussion instrument called the "Dappu" (a frame drum). (डप्पू नृत्य — आंध्र प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dappu dance is usually performed during festivals, fairs and processions, with energetic, synchronised movements.

• The classical dance of Andhra Pradesh is Kuchipudi.

NOTE

• Folk dances by state: Dappu (Andhra Pradesh), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab), Chhau (Odisha/Jharkhand/Bengal), Garba (Gujarat), Bihu (Assam).

question: In its 279th report released in April 2023, the Law Commission of India has recommended the provision of which law to be retained?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedition Law.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In its 279th report (April 2023), the Law Commission of India recommended that the Sedition Law (Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code) should be retained, with certain amendments and safeguards. (राजद्रोह कानून — 279वीं रिपोर्ट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Section 124A (IPC) deals with sedition — bringing hatred/contempt or exciting disaffection against the government by law. (In the new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the provisions have been restructured.)

• The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory advisory body that recommends legal reforms to the government.

NOTE

• The sedition law was a subject of major debate regarding freedom of speech (Article 19(1)(a)) versus national security.

question: With reference to 'slash and burn' agriculture, which of the following names is NOT related to Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roca.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given names for "slash and burn (shifting) agriculture", "Roca" is NOT related to Odisha — it is the term used in Brazil. The Odisha-related local names include Podu / Koman / Bringa / Pama Dabi. (रोका — ब्राज़ील, ओडिशा से संबंधित नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Local names of shifting cultivation in India: Jhum (North-East), Podu (Odisha/Andhra), Bewar/Dahiya (MP), Kumari (Western Ghats), Penda (Chhattisgarh).

• Around the world: Roca (Brazil), Milpa (Mexico/Central America), Ladang (Indonesia/Malaysia), Ray (Vietnam).

NOTE

• In slash-and-burn farming, forest patches are cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years, then left fallow to regain fertility.

question: What was the amount earned by BCCI from the sale of five teams in the inaugural Women's Indian Premier League (WPL) in January 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹4,669.99 crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The BCCI earned about ₹4,669.99 crore from the sale of the five franchises (teams) of the inaugural Women's Premier League (WPL) in January 2023. (महिला प्रीमियर लीग — ₹4,669.99 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The five WPL teams are based in Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad (Gujarat) and Lucknow.

• The first edition of the WPL (2023) was won by the Mumbai Indians (women).

NOTE

• The BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India) is the governing body for cricket in India; it also runs the men's IPL, one of the richest cricket leagues in the world.

question: Epilepsy is a disorder that affects which of the following parts of the human body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brain cells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Epilepsy is a neurological disorder that affects the brain (nerve cells/neurons). It is characterised by recurrent seizures (fits) caused by sudden, abnormal electrical activity in the brain. (मिर्गी — मस्तिष्क कोशिकाएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Seizures may cause loss of consciousness, convulsions or unusual sensations.

• Epilepsy can often be controlled with medication; it is not contagious. This is a sensitive medical topic; the focus here is purely the factual organ affected.

NOTE

• The brain, spinal cord and nerves make up the nervous system. Other neurological conditions studied in exams include Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease.

question: Which of the following options has all vector quantities?
option_1: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Power
option_2: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Acceleration
option_3: Power, Momentum, Energy, Speed and Work
option_4: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration
solution_text:
The correct answer is Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. In Option 4, all five — Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration — are vector quantities. (सदिश राशियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Energy, Power, Speed and Work are scalar quantities (they have only magnitude), so Options 1, 2 and 3 are wrong because each contains at least one scalar (Energy/Power/Speed/Work).

• "Weight" is a force (mass × gravitational acceleration) and is therefore a vector.

NOTE

• Examples of vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, weight.

• Examples of scalars: distance, speed, mass, time, energy, work, power, temperature.

question: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2005.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) was passed in 2005 (and came into force in 2006). It was later renamed the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2009. (राष्ट्रीय ग्रामीण रोजगार गारंटी अधिनियम — 2005)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

• It is one of the world's largest social security / employment schemes and promotes the "Right to Work".

NOTE

• The scheme is demand-driven; if work is not provided within 15 days, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance. It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

question: According to Article _____, there shall be equality of opportunities for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 16 of the Constitution guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State. (अनुच्छेद 16 — लोक नियोजन में अवसर की समानता)

• It also allows reservation for backward classes not adequately represented in state services.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — Equality before law; Article 15 — Prohibition of discrimination; Article 17 — Abolition of untouchability; Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

• Articles 14 to 18 together constitute the Right to Equality (Part III, Fundamental Rights).

NOTE

• Article 16 is a Fundamental Right and is enforceable in court. It ensures a fair and merit-based system for government jobs (with permitted reservations).

question: In the PM-SVANidhi Scheme (2020), the urban street vendors are eligible to avail a Working Capital Loan up to 10,000 with a tenure of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 year.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the PM SVANidhi Scheme (2020), urban street vendors can avail an initial collateral-free Working Capital Loan of up to ₹10,000, repayable within a tenure of 1 year (in monthly instalments). (पीएम स्वनिधि — 1 वर्ष की अवधि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• On timely repayment, the vendor becomes eligible for higher loans of ₹20,000 and then ₹50,000.

• The scheme offers a 7% interest subsidy and incentives for digital transactions, and is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

NOTE

• "SVANidhi" = PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi. It was launched during the COVID-19 pandemic to help street vendors resume their livelihoods.

question: Mica is which type of mineral?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Non-metallic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mica is a non-metallic mineral. It is an excellent electrical insulator with high dielectric strength, and is widely used in the electrical and electronics industry. (अभ्रक — अधात्विक खनिज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India is a major producer of mica; major deposits are in Jharkhand, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan (the Koderma belt of Jharkhand is famous).

• Metallic minerals contain metals — ferrous (iron-based: iron ore, manganese) and non-ferrous (copper, bauxite, gold).

NOTE

• Non-metallic minerals include mica, limestone, gypsum, dolomite, salt and phosphate. Energy/fuel minerals include coal, petroleum and natural gas.

question: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Canada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of a "Quasi-Federal" (strong Centre) form of government, along with the residuary powers being vested in the Centre and the appointment of State Governors by the Centre, was borrowed by the Indian Constitution from Canada. (कनाडा — अर्ध-संघीय व्यवस्था)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• From Canada, India also borrowed the idea of a Federation with a strong Centre and the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

• India is described as a "Union of States" (Article 1) — indestructible union with a strong central tilt.

NOTE

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review (USA); Parliamentary system, Rule of Law (UK); Directive Principles (Ireland); Emergency provisions, Fundamental Duties (erstwhile USSR/others); Concurrent List (Australia).

question: Sahaswan gharana of Rampur was established by whom among the following personalities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rampur-Sahaswan gharana of Hindustani classical (Khayal) vocal music was established/founded by Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan. (रामपुर-सहसवान घराना — उस्ताद इनायत हुसैन खान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rampur-Sahaswan gharana is known for its clear voice production, rhythmic mastery and forceful taans.

• Famous exponents of this gharana include Ustad Mushtaq Hussain Khan, Ghulam Mustafa Khan and Rashid Khan.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Mewati and Rampur-Sahaswan.

question: Which of the following social organisations was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay (Mumbai). It was a Hindu reform movement that gave the call "Back to the Vedas" and opposed idol worship, casteism, child marriage and superstitions. (आर्य समाज — 1875, स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Swami Dayananda wrote "Satyarth Prakash (The Light of Truth)".

• The Arya Samaj promoted women's education, widow remarriage and the Shuddhi movement (reconversion). It set up DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) schools and colleges.

NOTE

• Other reform bodies: Brahmo Samaj (1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy), Prarthana Samaj (1867, Atmaram Pandurang), Satyashodhak Samaj (1873, Jyotiba Phule).

question: The name of the autobiography of Saina Nehwal is called:
option_2: Playing to win, my life on and off court
solution_text:
The correct answer is Playing to win, my life on and off court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The autobiography of the ace Indian badminton player Saina Nehwal is titled "Playing to Win: My Life On and Off Court". (साइना नेहवाल की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Saina Nehwal was the first Indian woman to reach World No. 1 in badminton and won a bronze medal at the 2012 London Olympics. She has received the Padma Bhushan and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

• "Unbreakable" is the autobiography of the boxer Mary Kom.

NOTE

• Sports autobiographies: "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "The Race of My Life" (Milkha Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "Ace Against Odds" (Sania Mirza).
